title: Trump Pauses Russia Sanctions, Drawing Criticism From Both Parties
summary:
President Donald Trump has paused a number of sanctions on Russia just two days before they were set to begin. Sanctions are penalties, such as limits on money and trade, that countries use to pressure another country to change its actions.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by Trump in September. They were meant to put pressure on Russia over its war in Ukraine. The law also targeted senior Russian figures, including President Vladimir Putin, as well as Russian banks and a group of ships that Russia uses to get around existing trade limits.

On Friday night, Trump signed an executive order saying that suspending some of the sanctions was in the US national interest. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the pause would last 60 days, so the administration can study how the sanctions might affect the US and world economy.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said it was unfortunate that the US decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions. He said they "could have helped enormously" in pressuring Russia to end the war. He also said Russian attacks overnight had hit 15 Ukrainian energy sites, causing power cuts in several regions.

A Russian envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, praised Trump's order. He said the sanctions would have caused "serious damage" to the US and global markets.

The decision drew criticism from lawmakers in both major US parties. Democrats such as Virginia Congressman Don Beyer said Trump was turning his back on Ukraine. Some Republicans also disagreed. Texas Senator Ted Cruz called it a mistake, and Texas Senator John Cornyn called it "reckless."

Relations between the US and Ukraine were already tense. Last week, the US agreed to a deal to import Russian diesel fuel, and Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.
why_it_matters: The decision shows how a president can change how a law passed by Congress is carried out, and it affects the pressure on Russia over its war in Ukraine.

background_read: Russia invaded Ukraine, and the two countries have been at war, with Ukraine asking other nations for help.
Sanctions are a tool countries use instead of fighting: they limit trade, banking or travel to put economic pressure on a government.
In the United States, Congress can pass sanctions as a law, while the president leads foreign policy and can issue executive orders.
Because Congress had passed these sanctions as a law, pausing them caused disagreement with many lawmakers.
